Witztum, MDSearch for more papers by this authorAuthor, Article, and Disclosure Informationhttps://doi.org/10.7326/0003-4819-109-7-597_2 SectionsAboutPDF ToolsAdd to favoritesDownload CitationsTrack CitationsPermissions ShareFacebookTwitterLinkedInRedditEmail ExcerptTo the Editor: We recently observed a case of severe rhabdomyolysis in a patient being treated with lovastatin and nicotinic acid. Our report of this case may be both instructive and beneficial to physicians treating patients with hyperlipidemia.In a 43-year-old white man with familial hypercholesterolemia, presumed Gilbert syndrome, and known coronary artery disease, lovastatin therapy was initiated in July 1985. Since August 1986, lovastatin, 40 mg, and colestipol, 10 g, both given twice daily, had been well tolerated. In March 1987, nicotinic acid was started at 200 mg, three times daily, to lower the cholesterol level further. All medications...Reference1. NormanIllingsworthMunsonHsenpud DDJJ.
